children: Webull was fined $4.2 million by Finra for violations of anti-money-laundering, identity theft protection, and best execution rules, the brokerage industry's self-regulatory organization said Thursday.

Finra said Webull's supervisory systems failed to keep pace with the brokerage firm's rapid growth from 2020 to 2023. Webull failed, for example, to identify hundreds of unauthorized automated clearing house transfers, Finra said.

The company accepted and consented to Finra's findings without admitting or denying them, according to Finra's regulatory order. Webull also agreed to Finra's order that it remedy deficiencies in its anti-money-laundering and identity theft prevention programs, according to the order. A representative for Webull didn't respond to a request for comment.
Shares of Webull were down 7.5% Thursday morning amid a broad selloff in stocks. The S&P 500 was down 3.5%. The Vanguard Financials ETF, which tracks a basket of financial stocks, was down 0.8%.
Webull currently operates in 18 markets and has 29 million registered users.

Like rival Robinhood Markets, Webull's free stock-trading app soared in popularity during the pandemic and meme stock craze. Between January 2020 and September 2023, Webull approved the opening of at least 7 million new customer accounts, according to Finra.

For many new customer accounts, Webull relied on outside vendors to help with identity verification. But Webull didn't always have a reasonable basis to believe it knew who its new customers were, according to Finra. For example, Webull approved accounts for more than 50 customers who submitted photos of scenic landscapes instead of government-issued identification, Finra says. Webull also approved accounts for customers despite information Webull had in hand that the customers were deceased, Finra says.

Webull also failed to detect and report suspicious transactions, according to Finra, which says the brokerage firm failed to identify or investigate 473 unauthorized ACH transfers used to move over $1.5 million in assets from customers at other financial institutions into Webull accounts. The regulatory organization adds that Webull lacked surveillance capabilities essential for identifying fraudulent activities.

In addition, Webull's identity theft prevention program was flawed and didn't catch certain red flags, Finra says. And the regulator dinged Webull for lapses in best execution, saying the brokerage firm didn't conduct regular and rigorous reviews of customers' execution quality.

Last year, Fined fined Weibull $1.6 million, accusing the brokerage firm of not supervising social media posts by influencers who were promoting the firm and making statements that Finra said were unfair or exaggerated, among other claims.
